newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African miner Maranda to list on JSE Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: S.African miner Maranda to list on JSE Wednesday.

text.p: The reverse listing of junior zinc-copper mine Maranda Mining Co on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) was approved by Rooiberg Tin Ltd shareholders on Monday, the company said.
Rooiberg Tin is acquiring Maranda for 84 million rand, paving the way for its listing from May 14.
Rooiberg ceased mining in 1993 after a collapse in tin prices in the mid-1980s hit the firm. Listed-Rooiberg was placed in the Curtailed Operations sector of the JSE.
Following the takeover, the company will be placed back in the Metals and Minerals JSE sector and change its name to Maranda Mines Ltd.
Maranda is a zinc and copper mine in South Africa's Northern Province. The high grade deposit yields 15,000 tons of zinc and 1,500 tons of copper annually.
The firm also holds mineral rights over about 80 percent of the strike length of the zinc-copper line in the Murchison Range area.
The group commissioned its second shaft, called Romotshidi, last year and it is now nearing full production. A feasibility study on a third deposit, called Letaba, is also being finalised.
Maranda also aims to expand into the rest of the Southern African region and is a member of a consortium bidding for Zambia's Chibuluma copper mine.
